extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Salmonellosis (non-typhoidal Salmonella).

deaths: human deaths attributed to Salmonella infection (may require clinical adjudication)
hospitalizations: persons admitted to inpatient hospital care due to Salmonella illness

FoodNet incidence rates are population-based estimates, not raw national case counts — note denominator
Multistate outbreak case counts may be updated retroactively — capture report date and version
State-level case counts may include both outbreak-associated and sporadic cases — distinguish where possible
'Probable' and 'suspected' case definitions vary by jurisdiction — document source case definition
Animal/environmental Salmonella detections must not be counted as human cases

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Salmonellosis (non-typhoidal Salmonella).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC outbreak investigation pages, CDC FoodNet surveillance reports, and CDC PulseNet cluster announcements reporting Salmonella human cases, hospitalizations, and deaths in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC is the primary US federal public health authority for Salmonella surveillance. FoodNet provides active case counts; PulseNet tracks WGS-linked clusters; outbreak investigation pages provide serotype-specific case, hospitalization, and death counts with dates and locations.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify FDA CFSAN outbreak and food safety alert pages that report human illness counts, hospitalizations, and deaths linked to Salmonella-contaminated food products recalled or investigated during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FDA CFSAN publishes outbreak investigation pages with case counts, states affected, and illness date ranges for foodborne Salmonella events, often complementing CDC data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state health department situation reports, press releases, and epidemiological bulletins from US states reporting Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, or deaths during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, Texas DSHS, Florida DOH) publish subnational Salmonella data that may not be aggregated at the federal level within the task time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify USDA FSIS outbreak investigation reports that include human illness case counts linked to meat, poultry, or egg products during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: USDA FSIS investigates Salmonella outbreaks linked to FSIS-regulated products and publishes human illness counts alongside recall notices.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO PAHO situation reports or event-based surveillance summaries covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during 2024 for independent cross-validation of case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO and WHO publish regional disease event summaries that can serve as independent validation against CDC-reported figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) data or summary tables for Salmonella outbreaks reported in 2024 to cross-validate outbreak-level case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NORS is a structured database of US foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks; its aggregate counts can validate individual outbreak records collected from other sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definition documents and FoodNet methodology pages to clarify count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected) and reporting lag for Salmonella surveillance in the US.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC case definitions and FoodNet active surveillance methodology is essential for correctly classifying extracted counts into the appropriate schema fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature (PubMed/MMWR) reporting Salmonella outbreak investigations or surveillance summaries for the United States in 2024 to provide epidemiological context and case definition clarity.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MMWR reports and peer-reviewed outbreak investigations provide detailed case definitions, serotype data, and epidemiological curves that contextualize extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation report sources (e.g., Outbreak News Today, Food Safety News, ProMED) covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during May–July 2024 to surface outbreak signals not yet reflected in official sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and situation reports may capture early outbreak signals, state-level case counts, or recall-linked illness data before official CDC pages are published.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (e.g., cumulative vs. newly reported), where the reporting period substantially exceeds May–July 2024, or where Salmonella counts may include typhoidal serotypes, for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Ambiguous count semantics, broad reporting periods, and typhoidal contamination are the primary risks for incorrect record extraction in this task.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC Division of Foodborne, Waterborne, and Environmental Diseases (DFWED) publishes multistate Salmonella outbreak investigation pages with serotype, case counts, hospitalization counts, death counts, illness date ranges, and states affected. These are the highest-priority collection sources for the task.

CDC FoodNet (Foodborne Diseases Active Surveillance Network) provides active laboratory-confirmed Salmonella case counts across 10 US sites. Annual and preliminary reports may contain 2024 data covering the task window.
CDC PulseNet tracks WGS-linked Salmonella clusters and publishes cluster announcements with case counts and states affected. Relevant for identifying outbreak-linked confirmed case counts.
FDA CFSAN outbreak investigation pages report human illness counts, hospitalizations, and deaths linked to Salmonella-contaminated FDA-regulated food products. Often published alongside food recalls.

US state health departments publish Salmonella outbreak reports, press releases, and epidemiological bulletins with subnational case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths. Key states include CA, TX, FL, NY, GA, WA, and others with high Salmonella burden.
USDA FSIS publishes outbreak investigation reports and recall notices for Salmonella linked to meat, poultry, and egg products, including human illness counts.
PAHO and WHO publish regional disease event summaries and situation reports that may include US Salmonella outbreak data for independent cross-validation.
CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) is a structured database of US foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks with case, hospitalization, and death counts by pathogen, year, and state.

CDC MMWR reports and peer-reviewed outbreak investigations provide detailed Salmonella case definitions, serotype data, epidemiological curves, and case/death counts for US outbreaks. MMWR is the primary rapid communication vehicle for US outbreak investigations.

Reputable food safety and outbreak news sources (Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, ProMED) may surface early Salmonella outbreak signals, state-level case counts, and recall-linked illness data before official CDC pages are finalized.

disease_intelligence.suggested_geographic_granularity: state, county, city/locality (multistate outbreaks should be disaggregated by state where possible)
disease_intelligence.suggested_time_granularity: weekly or monthly (align with CDC NNDSS weekly tables and FoodNet reporting periods; use date_reported or date_of_illness_onset where available)
count_semantics_notes: cases_confirmed: laboratory-confirmed human Salmonella cases (culture or CIDT-positive with serotyping)
cases_probable: meets clinical criteria with epidemiological linkage but no lab confirmation
cases_suspected: clinical presentation consistent with Salmonella, no lab confirmation, no epi-link
cases_unspecified: reported case counts where confirmation status is not specified by source
deaths: human deaths attributed to Salmonella infection (may require clinical adjudication)
hospitalizations: persons admitted to inpatient hospital care due to Salmonella illness
Do NOT count food product positives, animal cases, or environmental detections as human cases
Multistate outbreak totals should be disaggregated by state if source permits
disambiguation_risks: Salmonella typhi (typhoid fever) must be excluded — this profile covers non-typhoidal Salmonella (NTS) only
CIDT-positive cases may be reported separately from culture-confirmed cases — distinguish in case_count fields
Recall-associated case counts may differ from epidemiologically confirmed outbreak case counts
FoodNet incidence rates are population-based estimates, not raw national case counts — note denominator
Multistate outbreak case counts may be updated retroactively — capture report date and version
State-level case counts may include both outbreak-associated and sporadic cases — distinguish where possible
'Probable' and 'suspected' case definitions vary by jurisdiction — document source case definition
Animal/environmental Salmonella detections must not be counted as human cases

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Salmonellosis (non-typhoidal Salmonella).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC outbreak investigation pages, CDC FoodNet surveillance reports, and CDC PulseNet cluster announcements reporting Salmonella human cases, hospitalizations, and deaths in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC is the primary US federal public health authority for Salmonella surveillance. FoodNet provides active case counts; PulseNet tracks WGS-linked clusters; outbreak investigation pages provide serotype-specific case, hospitalization, and death counts with dates and locations.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify FDA CFSAN outbreak and food safety alert pages that report human illness counts, hospitalizations, and deaths linked to Salmonella-contaminated food products recalled or investigated during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FDA CFSAN publishes outbreak investigation pages with case counts, states affected, and illness date ranges for foodborne Salmonella events, often complementing CDC data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state health department situation reports, press releases, and epidemiological bulletins from US states reporting Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, or deaths during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, Texas DSHS, Florida DOH) publish subnational Salmonella data that may not be aggregated at the federal level within the task time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify USDA FSIS outbreak investigation reports that include human illness case counts linked to meat, poultry, or egg products during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: USDA FSIS investigates Salmonella outbreaks linked to FSIS-regulated products and publishes human illness counts alongside recall notices.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO PAHO situation reports or event-based surveillance summaries covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during 2024 for independent cross-validation of case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO and WHO publish regional disease event summaries that can serve as independent validation against CDC-reported figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) data or summary tables for Salmonella outbreaks reported in 2024 to cross-validate outbreak-level case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NORS is a structured database of US foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks; its aggregate counts can validate individual outbreak records collected from other sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definition documents and FoodNet methodology pages to clarify count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected) and reporting lag for Salmonella surveillance in the US.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC case definitions and FoodNet active surveillance methodology is essential for correctly classifying extracted counts into the appropriate schema fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature (PubMed/MMWR) reporting Salmonella outbreak investigations or surveillance summaries for the United States in 2024 to provide epidemiological context and case definition clarity.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MMWR reports and peer-reviewed outbreak investigations provide detailed case definitions, serotype data, and epidemiological curves that contextualize extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation report sources (e.g., Outbreak News Today, Food Safety News, ProMED) covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during May–July 2024 to surface outbreak signals not yet reflected in official sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and situation reports may capture early outbreak signals, state-level case counts, or recall-linked illness data before official CDC pages are published.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (e.g., cumulative vs. newly reported), where the reporting period substantially exceeds May–July 2024, or where Salmonella counts may include typhoidal serotypes, for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Ambiguous count semantics, broad reporting periods, and typhoidal contamination are the primary risks for incorrect record extraction in this task.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC Division of Foodborne, Waterborne, and Environmental Diseases (DFWED) publishes multistate Salmonella outbreak investigation pages with serotype, case counts, hospitalization counts, death counts, illness date ranges, and states affected. These are the highest-priority collection sources for the task.

CDC FoodNet (Foodborne Diseases Active Surveillance Network) provides active laboratory-confirmed Salmonella case counts across 10 US sites. Annual and preliminary reports may contain 2024 data covering the task window.
CDC PulseNet tracks WGS-linked Salmonella clusters and publishes cluster announcements with case counts and states affected. Relevant for identifying outbreak-linked confirmed case counts.
FDA CFSAN outbreak investigation pages report human illness counts, hospitalizations, and deaths linked to Salmonella-contaminated FDA-regulated food products. Often published alongside food recalls.

US state health departments publish Salmonella outbreak reports, press releases, and epidemiological bulletins with subnational case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths. Key states include CA, TX, FL, NY, GA, WA, and others with high Salmonella burden.
USDA FSIS publishes outbreak investigation reports and recall notices for Salmonella linked to meat, poultry, and egg products, including human illness counts.
PAHO and WHO publish regional disease event summaries and situation reports that may include US Salmonella outbreak data for independent cross-validation.
CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) is a structured database of US foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks with case, hospitalization, and death counts by pathogen, year, and state.

CDC MMWR reports and peer-reviewed outbreak investigations provide detailed Salmonella case definitions, serotype data, epidemiological curves, and case/death counts for US outbreaks. MMWR is the primary rapid communication vehicle for US outbreak investigations.

Reputable food safety and outbreak news sources (Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, ProMED) may surface early Salmonella outbreak signals, state-level case counts, and recall-linked illness data before official CDC pages are finalized.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC outbreak investigation pages, CDC FoodNet surveillance reports, and CDC PulseNet cluster announcements reporting Salmonella human cases, hospitalizations, and deaths in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC is the primary US federal public health authority for Salmonella surveillance. FoodNet provides active case counts; PulseNet tracks WGS-linked clusters; outbreak investigation pages provide serotype-specific case, hospitalization, and death counts with dates and locations.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify FDA CFSAN outbreak and food safety alert pages that report human illness counts, hospitalizations, and deaths linked to Salmonella-contaminated food products recalled or investigated during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FDA CFSAN publishes outbreak investigation pages with case counts, states affected, and illness date ranges for foodborne Salmonella events, often complementing CDC data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state health department situation reports, press releases, and epidemiological bulletins from US states reporting Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, or deaths during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, Texas DSHS, Florida DOH) publish subnational Salmonella data that may not be aggregated at the federal level within the task time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify USDA FSIS outbreak investigation reports that include human illness case counts linked to meat, poultry, or egg products during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: USDA FSIS investigates Salmonella outbreaks linked to FSIS-regulated products and publishes human illness counts alongside recall notices.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO PAHO situation reports or event-based surveillance summaries covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during 2024 for independent cross-validation of case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO and WHO publish regional disease event summaries that can serve as independent validation against CDC-reported figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) data or summary tables for Salmonella outbreaks reported in 2024 to cross-validate outbreak-level case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NORS is a structured database of US foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks; its aggregate counts can validate individual outbreak records collected from other sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definition documents and FoodNet methodology pages to clarify count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected) and reporting lag for Salmonella surveillance in the US.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC case definitions and FoodNet active surveillance methodology is essential for correctly classifying extracted counts into the appropriate schema fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature (PubMed/MMWR) reporting Salmonella outbreak investigations or surveillance summaries for the United States in 2024 to provide epidemiological context and case definition clarity.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MMWR reports and peer-reviewed outbreak investigations provide detailed case definitions, serotype data, and epidemiological curves that contextualize extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation report sources (e.g., Outbreak News Today, Food Safety News, ProMED) covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during May–July 2024 to surface outbreak signals not yet reflected in official sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and situation reports may capture early outbreak signals, state-level case counts, or recall-linked illness data before official CDC pages are published.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (e.g., cumulative vs. newly reported), where the reporting period substantially exceeds May–July 2024, or where Salmonella counts may include typhoidal serotypes, for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Ambiguous count semantics, broad reporting periods, and typhoidal contamination are the primary risks for incorrect record extraction in this task.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC Division of Foodborne, Waterborne, and Environmental Diseases (DFWED) publishes multistate Salmonella outbreak investigation pages with serotype, case counts, hospitalization counts, death counts, illness date ranges, and states affected. These are the highest-priority collection sources for the task.

CDC FoodNet (Foodborne Diseases Active Surveillance Network) provides active laboratory-confirmed Salmonella case counts across 10 US sites. Annual and preliminary reports may contain 2024 data covering the task window.
CDC PulseNet tracks WGS-linked Salmonella clusters and publishes cluster announcements with case counts and states affected. Relevant for identifying outbreak-linked confirmed case counts.
FDA CFSAN outbreak investigation pages report human illness counts, hospitalizations, and deaths linked to Salmonella-contaminated FDA-regulated food products. Often published alongside food recalls.

US state health departments publish Salmonella outbreak reports, press releases, and epidemiological bulletins with subnational case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths. Key states include CA, TX, FL, NY, GA, WA, and others with high Salmonella burden.
USDA FSIS publishes outbreak investigation reports and recall notices for Salmonella linked to meat, poultry, and egg products, including human illness counts.
PAHO and WHO publish regional disease event summaries and situation reports that may include US Salmonella outbreak data for independent cross-validation.
CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) is a structured database of US foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks with case, hospitalization, and death counts by pathogen, year, and state.

CDC MMWR reports and peer-reviewed outbreak investigations provide detailed Salmonella case definitions, serotype data, epidemiological curves, and case/death counts for US outbreaks. MMWR is the primary rapid communication vehicle for US outbreak investigations.

Reputable food safety and outbreak news sources (Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, ProMED) may surface early Salmonella outbreak signals, state-level case counts, and recall-linked illness data before official CDC pages are finalized.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC outbreak investigation pages, CDC FoodNet surveillance reports, and CDC PulseNet cluster announcements reporting Salmonella human cases, hospitalizations, and deaths in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC is the primary US federal public health authority for Salmonella surveillance. FoodNet provides active case counts; PulseNet tracks WGS-linked clusters; outbreak investigation pages provide serotype-specific case, hospitalization, and death counts with dates and locations.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify FDA CFSAN outbreak and food safety alert pages that report human illness counts, hospitalizations, and deaths linked to Salmonella-contaminated food products recalled or investigated during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FDA CFSAN publishes outbreak investigation pages with case counts, states affected, and illness date ranges for foodborne Salmonella events, often complementing CDC data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state health department situation reports, press releases, and epidemiological bulletins from US states reporting Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, or deaths during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, Texas DSHS, Florida DOH) publish subnational Salmonella data that may not be aggregated at the federal level within the task time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify USDA FSIS outbreak investigation reports that include human illness case counts linked to meat, poultry, or egg products during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: USDA FSIS investigates Salmonella outbreaks linked to FSIS-regulated products and publishes human illness counts alongside recall notices.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO PAHO situation reports or event-based surveillance summaries covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during 2024 for independent cross-validation of case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO and WHO publish regional disease event summaries that can serve as independent validation against CDC-reported figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) data or summary tables for Salmonella outbreaks reported in 2024 to cross-validate outbreak-level case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NORS is a structured database of US foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks; its aggregate counts can validate individual outbreak records collected from other sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definition documents and FoodNet methodology pages to clarify count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected) and reporting lag for Salmonella surveillance in the US.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC case definitions and FoodNet active surveillance methodology is essential for correctly classifying extracted counts into the appropriate schema fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature (PubMed/MMWR) reporting Salmonella outbreak investigations or surveillance summaries for the United States in 2024 to provide epidemiological context and case definition clarity.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MMWR reports and peer-reviewed outbreak investigations provide detailed case definitions, serotype data, and epidemiological curves that contextualize extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation report sources (e.g., Outbreak News Today, Food Safety News, ProMED) covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during May–July 2024 to surface outbreak signals not yet reflected in official sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and situation reports may capture early outbreak signals, state-level case counts, or recall-linked illness data before official CDC pages are published.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (e.g., cumulative vs. newly reported), where the reporting period substantially exceeds May–July 2024, or where Salmonella counts may include typhoidal serotypes, for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Ambiguous count semantics, broad reporting periods, and typhoidal contamination are the primary risks for incorrect record extraction in this task.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC Division of Foodborne, Waterborne, and Environmental Diseases (DFWED) publishes multistate Salmonella outbreak investigation pages with serotype, case counts, hospitalization counts, death counts, illness date ranges, and states affected. These are the highest-priority collection sources for the task.

CDC FoodNet (Foodborne Diseases Active Surveillance Network) provides active laboratory-confirmed Salmonella case counts across 10 US sites. Annual and preliminary reports may contain 2024 data covering the task window.
CDC PulseNet tracks WGS-linked Salmonella clusters and publishes cluster announcements with case counts and states affected. Relevant for identifying outbreak-linked confirmed case counts.
FDA CFSAN outbreak investigation pages report human illness counts, hospitalizations, and deaths linked to Salmonella-contaminated FDA-regulated food products. Often published alongside food recalls.

US state health departments publish Salmonella outbreak reports, press releases, and epidemiological bulletins with subnational case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths. Key states include CA, TX, FL, NY, GA, WA, and others with high Salmonella burden.
USDA FSIS publishes outbreak investigation reports and recall notices for Salmonella linked to meat, poultry, and egg products, including human illness counts.
PAHO and WHO publish regional disease event summaries and situation reports that may include US Salmonella outbreak data for independent cross-validation.
CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) is a structured database of US foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks with case, hospitalization, and death counts by pathogen, year, and state.

CDC MMWR reports and peer-reviewed outbreak investigations provide detailed Salmonella case definitions, serotype data, epidemiological curves, and case/death counts for US outbreaks. MMWR is the primary rapid communication vehicle for US outbreak investigations.

Reputable food safety and outbreak news sources (Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, ProMED) may surface early Salmonella outbreak signals, state-level case counts, and recall-linked illness data before official CDC pages are finalized.

count_semantics_notes: cases_confirmed: laboratory-confirmed human Salmonella cases (culture or CIDT-positive with serotyping)
cases_probable: meets clinical criteria with epidemiological linkage but no lab confirmation
cases_suspected: clinical presentation consistent with Salmonella, no lab confirmation, no epi-link
cases_unspecified: reported case counts where confirmation status is not specified by source
deaths: human deaths attributed to Salmonella infection (may require clinical adjudication)
hospitalizations: persons admitted to inpatient hospital care due to Salmonella illness

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC outbreak investigation pages, CDC FoodNet surveillance reports, and CDC PulseNet cluster announcements reporting Salmonella human cases, hospitalizations, and deaths in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC is the primary US federal public health authority for Salmonella surveillance. FoodNet provides active case counts; PulseNet tracks WGS-linked clusters; outbreak investigation pages provide serotype-specific case, hospitalization, and death counts with dates and locations.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify FDA CFSAN outbreak and food safety alert pages that report human illness counts, hospitalizations, and deaths linked to Salmonella-contaminated food products recalled or investigated during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FDA CFSAN publishes outbreak investigation pages with case counts, states affected, and illness date ranges for foodborne Salmonella events, often complementing CDC data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state health department situation reports, press releases, and epidemiological bulletins from US states reporting Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, or deaths during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, Texas DSHS, Florida DOH) publish subnational Salmonella data that may not be aggregated at the federal level within the task time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify USDA FSIS outbreak investigation reports that include human illness case counts linked to meat, poultry, or egg products during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: USDA FSIS investigates Salmonella outbreaks linked to FSIS-regulated products and publishes human illness counts alongside recall notices.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO PAHO situation reports or event-based surveillance summaries covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during 2024 for independent cross-validation of case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO and WHO publish regional disease event summaries that can serve as independent validation against CDC-reported figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) data or summary tables for Salmonella outbreaks reported in 2024 to cross-validate outbreak-level case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NORS is a structured database of US foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks; its aggregate counts can validate individual outbreak records collected from other sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definition documents and FoodNet methodology pages to clarify count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected) and reporting lag for Salmonella surveillance in the US.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC case definitions and FoodNet active surveillance methodology is essential for correctly classifying extracted counts into the appropriate schema fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature (PubMed/MMWR) reporting Salmonella outbreak investigations or surveillance summaries for the United States in 2024 to provide epidemiological context and case definition clarity.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MMWR reports and peer-reviewed outbreak investigations provide detailed case definitions, serotype data, and epidemiological curves that contextualize extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation report sources (e.g., Outbreak News Today, Food Safety News, ProMED) covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during May–July 2024 to surface outbreak signals not yet reflected in official sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and situation reports may capture early outbreak signals, state-level case counts, or recall-linked illness data before official CDC pages are published.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (e.g., cumulative vs. newly reported), where the reporting period substantially exceeds May–July 2024, or where Salmonella counts may include typhoidal serotypes, for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Ambiguous count semantics, broad reporting periods, and typhoidal contamination are the primary risks for incorrect record extraction in this task.

iterative_search_queries.query: CDC Salmonella outbreak investigation 2024 cases hospitalizations deaths site:cdc.gov
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: CDC's outbreak investigation pages are the primary authoritative source for confirmed US Salmonella case counts, hospitalization rates, death counts, and subnational location breakdowns. Restricting to cdc.gov maximises precision. Removing rigid quoted phrases allows the query to match CDC's own page titles (e.g., 'Outbreak Investigation of Salmonella: [Vehicle] (Month Year)').

iterative_search_queries.query: Salmonella outbreak United States cases hospitalizations 2024 May June July site:cdc.gov OR site:fda.gov

iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: fda.gov or cdc.gov domain; official outbreak advisory or recall notice language; case count and hospitalization figures

iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: State .gov domain (e.g., health.state.xx.us or dph.xx.gov); official press release or advisory language; epidemiologic data table

iterative_search_queries.query: Salmonella outbreak US 2024 cases deaths recalled food ProMED OR "outbreak news" OR "food safety news"

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Salmonellosis (non-typhoidal Salmonella).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC outbreak investigation pages, CDC FoodNet surveillance reports, and CDC PulseNet cluster announcements reporting Salmonella human cases, hospitalizations, and deaths in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC is the primary US federal public health authority for Salmonella surveillance. FoodNet provides active case counts; PulseNet tracks WGS-linked clusters; outbreak investigation pages provide serotype-specific case, hospitalization, and death counts with dates and locations.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify FDA CFSAN outbreak and food safety alert pages that report human illness counts, hospitalizations, and deaths linked to Salmonella-contaminated food products recalled or investigated during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FDA CFSAN publishes outbreak investigation pages with case counts, states affected, and illness date ranges for foodborne Salmonella events, often complementing CDC data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state health department situation reports, press releases, and epidemiological bulletins from US states reporting Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, or deaths during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, Texas DSHS, Florida DOH) publish subnational Salmonella data that may not be aggregated at the federal level within the task time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify USDA FSIS outbreak investigation reports that include human illness case counts linked to meat, poultry, or egg products during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: USDA FSIS investigates Salmonella outbreaks linked to FSIS-regulated products and publishes human illness counts alongside recall notices.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO PAHO situation reports or event-based surveillance summaries covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during 2024 for independent cross-validation of case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO and WHO publish regional disease event summaries that can serve as independent validation against CDC-reported figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) data or summary tables for Salmonella outbreaks reported in 2024 to cross-validate outbreak-level case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NORS is a structured database of US foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks; its aggregate counts can validate individual outbreak records collected from other sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definition documents and FoodNet methodology pages to clarify count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected) and reporting lag for Salmonella surveillance in the US.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC case definitions and FoodNet active surveillance methodology is essential for correctly classifying extracted counts into the appropriate schema fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature (PubMed/MMWR) reporting Salmonella outbreak investigations or surveillance summaries for the United States in 2024 to provide epidemiological context and case definition clarity.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MMWR reports and peer-reviewed outbreak investigations provide detailed case definitions, serotype data, and epidemiological curves that contextualize extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation report sources (e.g., Outbreak News Today, Food Safety News, ProMED) covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during May–July 2024 to surface outbreak signals not yet reflected in official sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and situation reports may capture early outbreak signals, state-level case counts, or recall-linked illness data before official CDC pages are published.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (e.g., cumulative vs. newly reported), where the reporting period substantially exceeds May–July 2024, or where Salmonella counts may include typhoidal serotypes, for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Ambiguous count semantics, broad reporting periods, and typhoidal contamination are the primary risks for incorrect record extraction in this task.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC Division of Foodborne, Waterborne, and Environmental Diseases (DFWED) publishes multistate Salmonella outbreak investigation pages with serotype, case counts, hospitalization counts, death counts, illness date ranges, and states affected. These are the highest-priority collection sources for the task.

CDC FoodNet (Foodborne Diseases Active Surveillance Network) provides active laboratory-confirmed Salmonella case counts across 10 US sites. Annual and preliminary reports may contain 2024 data covering the task window.
CDC PulseNet tracks WGS-linked Salmonella clusters and publishes cluster announcements with case counts and states affected. Relevant for identifying outbreak-linked confirmed case counts.
FDA CFSAN outbreak investigation pages report human illness counts, hospitalizations, and deaths linked to Salmonella-contaminated FDA-regulated food products. Often published alongside food recalls.

US state health departments publish Salmonella outbreak reports, press releases, and epidemiological bulletins with subnational case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths. Key states include CA, TX, FL, NY, GA, WA, and others with high Salmonella burden.
USDA FSIS publishes outbreak investigation reports and recall notices for Salmonella linked to meat, poultry, and egg products, including human illness counts.
PAHO and WHO publish regional disease event summaries and situation reports that may include US Salmonella outbreak data for independent cross-validation.
CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) is a structured database of US foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks with case, hospitalization, and death counts by pathogen, year, and state.

CDC MMWR reports and peer-reviewed outbreak investigations provide detailed Salmonella case definitions, serotype data, epidemiological curves, and case/death counts for US outbreaks. MMWR is the primary rapid communication vehicle for US outbreak investigations.

Reputable food safety and outbreak news sources (Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, ProMED) may surface early Salmonella outbreak signals, state-level case counts, and recall-linked illness data before official CDC pages are finalized.

FoodNet provides active case counts; PulseNet tracks WGS-linked clusters; outbreak investigation pages provide serotype-specific case, hospitalization, and death counts with dates and locations.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify FDA CFSAN outbreak and food safety alert pages that report human illness counts, hospitalizations, and deaths linked to Salmonella-contaminated food products recalled or investigated during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FDA CFSAN publishes outbreak investigation pages with case counts, states affected, and illness date ranges for foodborne Salmonella events, often complementing CDC data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state health department situation reports, press releases, and epidemiological bulletins from US states reporting Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, or deaths during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, Texas DSHS, Florida DOH) publish subnational Salmonella data that may not be aggregated at the federal level within the task time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify USDA FSIS outbreak investigation reports that include human illness case counts linked to meat, poultry, or egg products during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: USDA FSIS investigates Salmonella outbreaks linked to FSIS-regulated products and publishes human illness counts alongside recall notices.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO PAHO situation reports or event-based surveillance summaries covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during 2024 for independent cross-validation of case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO and WHO publish regional disease event summaries that can serve as independent validation against CDC-reported figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) data or summary tables for Salmonella outbreaks reported in 2024 to cross-validate outbreak-level case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NORS is a structured database of US foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks; its aggregate counts can validate individual outbreak records collected from other sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definition documents and FoodNet methodology pages to clarify count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected) and reporting lag for Salmonella surveillance in the US.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC case definitions and FoodNet active surveillance methodology is essential for correctly classifying extracted counts into the appropriate schema fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature (PubMed/MMWR) reporting Salmonella outbreak investigations or surveillance summaries for the United States in 2024 to provide epidemiological context and case definition clarity.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MMWR reports and peer-reviewed outbreak investigations provide detailed case definitions, serotype data, and epidemiological curves that contextualize extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation report sources (e.g., Outbreak News Today, Food Safety News, ProMED) covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during May–July 2024 to surface outbreak signals not yet reflected in official sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and situation reports may capture early outbreak signals, state-level case counts, or recall-linked illness data before official CDC pages are published.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (e.g., cumulative vs. newly reported), where the reporting period substantially exceeds May–July 2024, or where Salmonella counts may include typhoidal serotypes, for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Ambiguous count semantics, broad reporting periods, and typhoidal contamination are the primary risks for incorrect record extraction in this task.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC Division of Foodborne, Waterborne, and Environmental Diseases (DFWED) publishes multistate Salmonella outbreak investigation pages with serotype, case counts, hospitalization counts, death counts, illness date ranges, and states affected. These are the highest-priority collection sources for the task.

CDC FoodNet (Foodborne Diseases Active Surveillance Network) provides active laboratory-confirmed Salmonella case counts across 10 US sites. Annual and preliminary reports may contain 2024 data covering the task window.
CDC PulseNet tracks WGS-linked Salmonella clusters and publishes cluster announcements with case counts and states affected. Relevant for identifying outbreak-linked confirmed case counts.
FDA CFSAN outbreak investigation pages report human illness counts, hospitalizations, and deaths linked to Salmonella-contaminated FDA-regulated food products. Often published alongside food recalls.

US state health departments publish Salmonella outbreak reports, press releases, and epidemiological bulletins with subnational case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths. Key states include CA, TX, FL, NY, GA, WA, and others with high Salmonella burden.
USDA FSIS publishes outbreak investigation reports and recall notices for Salmonella linked to meat, poultry, and egg products, including human illness counts.
PAHO and WHO publish regional disease event summaries and situation reports that may include US Salmonella outbreak data for independent cross-validation.
CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) is a structured database of US foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks with case, hospitalization, and death counts by pathogen, year, and state.

CDC MMWR reports and peer-reviewed outbreak investigations provide detailed Salmonella case definitions, serotype data, epidemiological curves, and case/death counts for US outbreaks. MMWR is the primary rapid communication vehicle for US outbreak investigations.

Reputable food safety and outbreak news sources (Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, ProMED) may surface early Salmonella outbreak signals, state-level case counts, and recall-linked illness data before official CDC pages are finalized.

deaths: human deaths attributed to Salmonella infection (may require clinical adjudication)
hospitalizations: persons admitted to inpatient hospital care due to Salmonella illness

Multistate outbreak totals should be disaggregated by state if source permits

FoodNet incidence rates are population-based estimates, not raw national case counts — note denominator
Multistate outbreak case counts may be updated retroactively — capture report date and version
State-level case counts may include both outbreak-associated and sporadic cases — distinguish where possible
'Probable' and 'suspected' case definitions vary by jurisdiction — document source case definition
Animal/environmental Salmonella detections must not be counted as human cases

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC outbreak investigation pages, CDC FoodNet surveillance reports, and CDC PulseNet cluster announcements reporting Salmonella human cases, hospitalizations, and deaths in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC is the primary US federal public health authority for Salmonella surveillance. FoodNet provides active case counts; PulseNet tracks WGS-linked clusters; outbreak investigation pages provide serotype-specific case, hospitalization, and death counts with dates and locations.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify FDA CFSAN outbreak and food safety alert pages that report human illness counts, hospitalizations, and deaths linked to Salmonella-contaminated food products recalled or investigated during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FDA CFSAN publishes outbreak investigation pages with case counts, states affected, and illness date ranges for foodborne Salmonella events, often complementing CDC data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state health department situation reports, press releases, and epidemiological bulletins from US states reporting Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, or deaths during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, Texas DSHS, Florida DOH) publish subnational Salmonella data that may not be aggregated at the federal level within the task time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify USDA FSIS outbreak investigation reports that include human illness case counts linked to meat, poultry, or egg products during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: USDA FSIS investigates Salmonella outbreaks linked to FSIS-regulated products and publishes human illness counts alongside recall notices.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO PAHO situation reports or event-based surveillance summaries covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during 2024 for independent cross-validation of case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO and WHO publish regional disease event summaries that can serve as independent validation against CDC-reported figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) data or summary tables for Salmonella outbreaks reported in 2024 to cross-validate outbreak-level case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NORS is a structured database of US foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks; its aggregate counts can validate individual outbreak records collected from other sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definition documents and FoodNet methodology pages to clarify count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected) and reporting lag for Salmonella surveillance in the US.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC case definitions and FoodNet active surveillance methodology is essential for correctly classifying extracted counts into the appropriate schema fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature (PubMed/MMWR) reporting Salmonella outbreak investigations or surveillance summaries for the United States in 2024 to provide epidemiological context and case definition clarity.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MMWR reports and peer-reviewed outbreak investigations provide detailed case definitions, serotype data, and epidemiological curves that contextualize extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation report sources (e.g., Outbreak News Today, Food Safety News, ProMED) covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during May–July 2024 to surface outbreak signals not yet reflected in official sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and situation reports may capture early outbreak signals, state-level case counts, or recall-linked illness data before official CDC pages are published.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (e.g., cumulative vs. newly reported), where the reporting period substantially exceeds May–July 2024, or where Salmonella counts may include typhoidal serotypes, for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Ambiguous count semantics, broad reporting periods, and typhoidal contamination are the primary risks for incorrect record extraction in this task.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC Division of Foodborne, Waterborne, and Environmental Diseases (DFWED) publishes multistate Salmonella outbreak investigation pages with serotype, case counts, hospitalization counts, death counts, illness date ranges, and states affected. These are the highest-priority collection sources for the task.

CDC FoodNet (Foodborne Diseases Active Surveillance Network) provides active laboratory-confirmed Salmonella case counts across 10 US sites. Annual and preliminary reports may contain 2024 data covering the task window.
CDC PulseNet tracks WGS-linked Salmonella clusters and publishes cluster announcements with case counts and states affected. Relevant for identifying outbreak-linked confirmed case counts.
FDA CFSAN outbreak investigation pages report human illness counts, hospitalizations, and deaths linked to Salmonella-contaminated FDA-regulated food products. Often published alongside food recalls.

US state health departments publish Salmonella outbreak reports, press releases, and epidemiological bulletins with subnational case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths. Key states include CA, TX, FL, NY, GA, WA, and others with high Salmonella burden.
USDA FSIS publishes outbreak investigation reports and recall notices for Salmonella linked to meat, poultry, and egg products, including human illness counts.
PAHO and WHO publish regional disease event summaries and situation reports that may include US Salmonella outbreak data for independent cross-validation.
CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) is a structured database of US foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks with case, hospitalization, and death counts by pathogen, year, and state.

CDC MMWR reports and peer-reviewed outbreak investigations provide detailed Salmonella case definitions, serotype data, epidemiological curves, and case/death counts for US outbreaks. MMWR is the primary rapid communication vehicle for US outbreak investigations.

Reputable food safety and outbreak news sources (Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, ProMED) may surface early Salmonella outbreak signals, state-level case counts, and recall-linked illness data before official CDC pages are finalized.

iterative_search_queries.query: Salmonella outbreak 2024 cases hospitalizations "May 2024" OR "June 2024" OR "July 2024" site:cdc.gov
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Complements iter2_q1 by using quoted month-year phrases to match CDC pages that mention illness onset dates or report dates in the May–July 2024 window, even if the outbreak was named for a different month. This is particularly important for outbreaks like the Eggs September 2024 event (illness onset May 23) and any other outbreaks where the vehicle was identified later but illnesses began in the window.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC outbreak investigation page with illness onset dates or case-count update dates falling in May–July 2024; Fast Facts or investigation update table with numeric case/hospitalization/death data
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain; quoted date strings matching the target window; epidemiologic curve or case-count table

iterative_search_queries.query: Salmonella outbreak United States May June July 2024 cases hospitalizations deaths FDA advisory recall site:fda.gov OR site:fsis.usda.gov
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Iteration 1 returned only 3 fda.gov results and 1 fsis.usda.gov result, none with visible case counts in snippets. FDA outbreak advisories and FSIS public health alerts for Salmonella events in May–July 2024 are critical secondary authoritative sources that often include case counts, hospitalization figures, and state distributions not yet captured. FSIS covers meat/poultry Salmonella events specifically.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: FDA outbreak advisory or FSIS public health alert dated May–July 2024 with Salmonella case counts, states affected, and illness date range; recall notice linking to CDC case data
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: fda.gov or fsis.usda.gov domain; official outbreak advisory or public health alert language; case count and hospitalization figures; publication date May–July 2024

iterative_search_queries.query: Salmonella outbreak United States 2024 cases deaths hospitalizations "state" "confirmed" "May" OR "June" OR "July" site:foodsafetynews.com OR site:cidrap.umn.edu OR site:outbreaknewstoday.com
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Food Safety News, CIDRAP, and Outbreak News Today are the highest-quality specialist news sources for US Salmonella outbreak coverage. They routinely publish state-level case breakdowns, hospitalization figures, and probable/suspected case counts that are absent from CDC federal summaries. CIDRAP appeared twice in iteration 1 but without visible case counts; targeting these domains directly with month-year terms maximises the chance of surfacing subnational data and filling the cases_probable/ca...[truncated]
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: Food Safety News or CIDRAP article dated May–July 2024 citing official case counts by state, hospitalization numbers, and death figures for a specific Salmonella outbreak; Outbreak News Today post with state-level breakdown
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: foodsafetynews.com, cidrap.umn.edu, or outbreaknewstoday.com domain; article publication date May–July 2024; direct citation of CDC or state health department figures; numeric case/hospitalization/death data

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Salmonellosis (non-typhoidal Salmonella).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC outbreak investigation pages, CDC FoodNet surveillance reports, and CDC PulseNet cluster announcements reporting Salmonella human cases, hospitalizations, and deaths in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC is the primary US federal public health authority for Salmonella surveillance. FoodNet provides active case counts; PulseNet tracks WGS-linked clusters; outbreak investigation pages provide serotype-specific case, hospitalization, and death counts with dates and locations.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify FDA CFSAN outbreak and food safety alert pages that report human illness counts, hospitalizations, and deaths linked to Salmonella-contaminated food products recalled or investigated during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FDA CFSAN publishes outbreak investigation pages with case counts, states affected, and illness date ranges for foodborne Salmonella events, often complementing CDC data.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state health department situation reports, press releases, and epidemiological bulletins from US states reporting Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, or deaths during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (e.g., California CDPH, Texas DSHS, Florida DOH) publish subnational Salmonella data that may not be aggregated at the federal level within the task time window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify USDA FSIS outbreak investigation reports that include human illness case counts linked to meat, poultry, or egg products during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: USDA FSIS investigates Salmonella outbreaks linked to FSIS-regulated products and publishes human illness counts alongside recall notices.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO PAHO situation reports or event-based surveillance summaries covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during 2024 for independent cross-validation of case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: PAHO and WHO publish regional disease event summaries that can serve as independent validation against CDC-reported figures.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) data or summary tables for Salmonella outbreaks reported in 2024 to cross-validate outbreak-level case and death counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: NORS is a structured database of US foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks; its aggregate counts can validate individual outbreak records collected from other sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definition documents and FoodNet methodology pages to clarify count semantics (confirmed vs. probable vs. suspected) and reporting lag for Salmonella surveillance in the US.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding CDC case definitions and FoodNet active surveillance methodology is essential for correctly classifying extracted counts into the appropriate schema fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature (PubMed/MMWR) reporting Salmonella outbreak investigations or surveillance summaries for the United States in 2024 to provide epidemiological context and case definition clarity.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MMWR reports and peer-reviewed outbreak investigations provide detailed case definitions, serotype data, and epidemiological curves that contextualize extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation report sources (e.g., Outbreak News Today, Food Safety News, ProMED) covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during May–July 2024 to surface outbreak signals not yet reflected in official sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News and situation reports may capture early outbreak signals, state-level case counts, or recall-linked illness data before official CDC pages are published.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources where count semantics are ambiguous (e.g., cumulative vs. newly reported), where the reporting period substantially exceeds May–July 2024, or where Salmonella counts may include typhoidal serotypes, for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Ambiguous count semantics, broad reporting periods, and typhoidal contamination are the primary risks for incorrect record extraction in this task.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC Division of Foodborne, Waterborne, and Environmental Diseases (DFWED) publishes multistate Salmonella outbreak investigation pages with serotype, case counts, hospitalization counts, death counts, illness date ranges, and states affected. These are the highest-priority collection sources for the task.

CDC FoodNet (Foodborne Diseases Active Surveillance Network) provides active laboratory-confirmed Salmonella case counts across 10 US sites. Annual and preliminary reports may contain 2024 data covering the task window.
CDC PulseNet tracks WGS-linked Salmonella clusters and publishes cluster announcements with case counts and states affected. Relevant for identifying outbreak-linked confirmed case counts.
FDA CFSAN outbreak investigation pages report human illness counts, hospitalizations, and deaths linked to Salmonella-contaminated FDA-regulated food products. Often published alongside food recalls.

US state health departments publish Salmonella outbreak reports, press releases, and epidemiological bulletins with subnational case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths. Key states include CA, TX, FL, NY, GA, WA, and others with high Salmonella burden.
USDA FSIS publishes outbreak investigation reports and recall notices for Salmonella linked to meat, poultry, and egg products, including human illness counts.
PAHO and WHO publish regional disease event summaries and situation reports that may include US Salmonella outbreak data for independent cross-validation.
CDC NORS (National Outbreak Reporting System) is a structured database of US foodborne and enteric disease outbreaks with case, hospitalization, and death counts by pathogen, year, and state.

CDC MMWR reports and peer-reviewed outbreak investigations provide detailed Salmonella case definitions, serotype data, epidemiological curves, and case/death counts for US outbreaks. MMWR is the primary rapid communication vehicle for US outbreak investigations.

Reputable food safety and outbreak news sources (Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, ProMED) may surface early Salmonella outbreak signals, state-level case counts, and recall-linked illness data before official CDC pages are finalized.

iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: FDA outbreak advisory or recall notice citing Salmonella case counts, states affected, and illness dates; CDC multistate outbreak page
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: fda.gov or cdc.gov domain; official outbreak advisory or recall notice language; case count and hospitalization figures

iterative_search_queries.query: Salmonella outbreak United States 2024 cases deaths hospitalizations state health department
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: State health departments (e.g., CDPH, NYSDOH, TXDSHS) often publish their own Salmonella outbreak advisories with subnational case counts, locality detail, and hospitalization figures before CDC finalises a multistate summary. A broad web search without domain restriction surfaces these state-level pages, which are critical for the subnational_location and locality target fields.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: State health department press release or outbreak advisory with case counts, county or city breakdown, and illness date range
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: State .gov domain (e.g., health.state.xx.us or dph.xx.gov); official press release or advisory language; epidemiologic data table

iterative_search_queries.query: Salmonella outbreak US 2024 cases deaths recalled food ProMED OR "outbreak news" OR "food safety news"
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: ProMED-mail and specialist food-safety news outlets (e.g., Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today) aggregate and cite official case counts, hospitalization data, and death figures for US Salmonella outbreaks, often with state-level granularity and earlier publication dates than CDC final summaries. This query covers the news/situation-report source type and may surface outbreaks not yet finalised on CDC pages.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: ProMED post or food-safety news article citing official case counts, states affected, hospitalization numbers, and death toll for a specific Salmonella outbreak event
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: ProMED archive post with DONs reference; Food Safety News or Outbreak News Today byline citing CDC or state health department figures; publication date within May–July 2024

iterative_search_queries.query: CDC Salmonella outbreak investigation June 2024 OR July 2024 cases hospitalizations deaths site:cdc.gov
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Iteration 1 surfaced the Backyard Poultry May 2024 outbreak but no CDC investigation pages specifically initiated in June or July 2024. This query directly targets CDC outbreak pages for those two months, which are the most underrepresented part of the window. The CDC 2024 summary mentions 38 Salmonella outbreaks — individual pages for June–July events are the highest-priority gap.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC outbreak investigation index or update page with title containing 'June 2024' or 'July 2024', listing case counts, states, hospitalizations, and deaths
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain; outbreak investigation page URL pattern /salmonella/outbreaks/[vehicle]-06-24/ or -07-24/; Fast Facts box with case/hospitalization/death counts

iterative_search_queries.query: Salmonella outbreak 2024 cases hospitalizations "May 2024" OR "June 2024" OR "July 2024" site:cdc.gov
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Complements iter2_q1 by using quoted month-year phrases to match CDC pages that mention illness onset dates or report dates in the May–July 2024 window, even if the outbreak was named for a different month. This is particularly important for outbreaks like the Eggs September 2024 event (illness onset May 23) and any other outbreaks where the vehicle was identified later but illnesses began in the window.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC outbreak investigation page with illness onset dates or case-count update dates falling in May–July 2024; Fast Facts or investigation update table with numeric case/hospitalization/death data
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain; quoted date strings matching the target window; epidemiologic curve or case-count table

iterative_search_queries.query: Salmonella outbreak United States May June July 2024 cases hospitalizations deaths FDA advisory recall site:fda.gov OR site:fsis.usda.gov
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Iteration 1 returned only 3 fda.gov results and 1 fsis.usda.gov result, none with visible case counts in snippets. FDA outbreak advisories and FSIS public health alerts for Salmonella events in May–July 2024 are critical secondary authoritative sources that often include case counts, hospitalization figures, and state distributions not yet captured. FSIS covers meat/poultry Salmonella events specifically.
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: FDA outbreak advisory or FSIS public health alert dated May–July 2024 with Salmonella case counts, states affected, and illness date range; recall notice linking to CDC case data
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: fda.gov or fsis.usda.gov domain; official outbreak advisory or public health alert language; case count and hospitalization figures; publication date May–July 2024

iterative_search_queries.query: Salmonella outbreak United States 2024 cases deaths hospitalizations "state" "confirmed" "May" OR "June" OR "July" site:foodsafetynews.com OR site:cidrap.umn.edu OR site:outbreaknewstoday.com
iterative_search_queries.query_rationale: Food Safety News, CIDRAP, and Outbreak News Today are the highest-quality specialist news sources for US Salmonella outbreak coverage. They routinely publish state-level case breakdowns, hospitalization figures, and probable/suspected case counts that are absent from CDC federal summaries. CIDRAP appeared twice in iteration 1 but without visible case counts; targeting these domains directly with month-year terms maximises the chance of surfacing subnational data and filling the cases_probable/ca...[truncated]
iterative_search_queries.expected_source_type_or_evidence: Food Safety News or CIDRAP article dated May–July 2024 citing official case counts by state, hospitalization numbers, and death figures for a specific Salmonella outbreak; Outbreak News Today post with state-level breakdown
iterative_search_queries.expected_trust_signal: foodsafetynews.com, cidrap.umn.edu, or outbreaknewstoday.com domain; article publication date May–July 2024; direct citation of CDC or state health department figures; numeric case/hospitalization/death data

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Salmonellosis (non-typhoidal Salmonella).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.
